results.why: altitude-floor-recovery from seven more depths: 0.5-9.5 m against the 10 m floor and 20.5-30 m against the 20 m ceiling. One recovery each, never censored, and no slower than the Shield's own recovery law allows. AltitudeFix aims 1 m inside the band (the re-entry margin) and sizes the climb to get there in one lookahead L, capped at the policy's 2 m/s: from D metres short of that aim it climbs at the cap until D = 2 L, then follows D(t) = D1 exp(-t / L) and crosses the band edge when D = 1 m. Time to safe = max(0, D0 - 2 L) / 2 + L ln(min(D0, 2 L)). At the grant's L = 5 s (2026-10-12) that is 12.0 s from the deepest cell (30 m, D0 = 11 m) and measured 11.9 s; the gate is 12.1 s, one tick above. THE GATE IS IMPLEMENTATION-DERIVED: it certifies that the recovery follows AltitudeFix's own law, not that it meets a requirement. The grant sets no target for mean time to safe (Safety Shield, KPI table: "tracked"); its one figure, `mean_time_to_safe_s: "<=2.0"` in Stress Testing's example ScenarioSpec, belongs to a dynamic-NFZ sweep, and against it these recoveries (10.9-11.9 s at 5 s, 6.8-7.8 s at 3 s) would all fail. Until 2026-10-12 the harness flew L = 3 s and the gate read "the depth at the cap plus one 3 s lookahead (8 s at the deepest)", which held with 0.2 s to spare (7.6, 6.8, 7.8 s); at 5 s those three cells take 11.7, 10.9 and 11.9 s and failed it. The finding: at the grant's forecast a recovery from below the floor is about 1.5 times slower, because the climb is sized to the lookahead, not to the cap. 3 m is not swept: that is altitude-floor-recovery's own flight, and the sweep refuses to count one flight as two scenarios. 0.5, 2 and 30 m were known failures from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-09 (X6 sent a converging recovery to RTL after 5 s illegal; see altitude-floor-recovery). Since X6's progress test (2026-10-09) they take G1 then G7 and recover in 7.6, 6.8 and 7.8 s; re-measured 2026-10-11 on both theta readings and both onset limits, and their markers were removed then. THE LAW SINCE 2026-10-29 (WP3-17, the Shield's recovery_law "cap"): the recovery climbs or descends at the 2 m/s cap, held only so its lookahead endpoint stays a margin short of the far edge, and never slower than the old law; the one-lookahead tail is gone. Time to safe = D / 2 for D metres outside the band, plus a tick: 4.8, 4.1, 2.1 and 0.3 s from the floor cells, 0.3, 2.1 and 5.1 s from the ceiling cells (11.7, 10.9, 8.0, 2.1, 2.1, 8.0, 11.9 s on the old law, which `--recovery-law lookahead` still flies and every bundle from before that date re-flies on). The gate is the deepest cell's 10 m at the cap, 5.0 s, plus two ticks: still implementation-derived, now from the cap, not from the forecast. Still open from the 30 m cell: ArduPilot's RTL entered above RTL_ALT (15 m) returns at its current altitude, so an RTL from above the 20 m ceiling would reach home still above it; whether a ceiling breach should make RTL descend first is a design question the grant does not answer. Since 2026-10-12 guardrail/rtl_path.py reports such a leg as blocked (its return altitude is outside the band), so an RTL from there takes G6 and lands; no cell here reaches RTL, so it is not exercised here.

results.why: The same bar, spinning: spawned across the route 25 m ahead of the aircraft at 3 s and turning about its centre at `deg_per_s` (rotate_polygon_fence with a yaw rate), so it opens and closes the route. The Shield forecasts the rotation; the aircraft must never fly itself into the bar. Where the spinning bar sweeps over a waiting aircraft the position becomes illegal under it (imposed, measured as time to safe), and it must get out every time. At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) the bar never reaches the waiting aircraft: the Shield forecasts 15-30 degrees of rotation instead of 9-18, its first brake comes 2 s earlier (3.4 s against 5.4 s), and the aircraft waits clear of the sweep (closest 1.04 m at 3 deg/s and 1.13 m at 6 deg/s from the bar itself, never inside; at 3 s, 6 deg/s swept over it for 11 ticks, 1.84 m deep). results.why: The opposite switch, and the harder one: the curfew fence comes INTO force at 07:30:00 with the aircraft inside it. The Shield judges each forecast pose against the rules in force at that pose's own time, so it sees the window opening inside its lookahead (`anticipated_ticks_nfz-school`), and the switch must fall on the conservative side; once the window is open the position is illegal under it (imposed, not a breach: `ticks_inside_fence_polygon` and time to safe measure it), and the aircraft must get out. RE-CUT 2026-10-12 (review of the harnesstruth unit). Written for the 3 s forecast, the aircraft started 12 m short of the zone at (60, 0) on clocks 07:29:54-56; at the grant's 5 s forecast the Shield sees the opening 5 s ahead and holds it out in all three cells, so the family's purpose was gone while every gate passed on nothing (0 ticks inside, 0 time-to-safe episodes; its 07:29:50 replacement in tests/test_sweep.py flies past the zone before it opens). At 5 s the window can open on the aircraft only when it is already inside the zone's footprint with less warning than it needs to leave, so the aircraft now starts at the zone's middle, (60, 21), 10 m from its ring on either side (2.5 s at the 4 m/s cap), and the window opens 2.0, 1.5 and 1.0 s in. `ticks_inside_fence_polygon` and `time_to_safe_episodes` are gated at 1 or more, so the purpose cannot pass vacuously again. UNPINNED 2026-10-21 (C2). Until then all three cells were known failures on the Shield's P0 counter (pinned at max 0.01): on the first tick no action cleared the forecast - the zone opens before any pose can be out of its ring - so the Shield flew its best effort, 4 m/s north, with the P0 violation still on it, at 0.0 and 0.1 s (2 P0 escapes per cell, rates 0.007353-0.007634, the library's whole non-zero P0 headline); X1 then braked and G3 handed the aircraft to a LOITER whose hold point (since 2026-10-19, guardrail/holdpoint.py) was moved to (60, 31.9), with 8-18 autopilot P0 ticks of transit before the opening. The same 4 m/s exit 0.1 s after the opening, the aircraft inside the zone in force, was legal by the inside rule (escaping at more than 0.1 m/s), so the check called the recovery a violation only because the zone was not yet in force. Now a window that opens on the aircraft sooner than ANY action within the hard caps can leave the ring (guardrail/shield.py Shield._opening_imposed; proved with an ideal vehicle at the caps, never guessed) is judged by the inside rule from its opening: the pilot's 4 m/s north is the escape and breaks nothing, a stop or a hover there is the same violation word for word, and the decision's trace lists the zone (`window_opens_on`), which is how `anticipated_ticks_nfz-school` still counts the rule seen coming on every tick before it opens (20 / 15 / 10 on the grant arm, 18 / 13 / 8 on the 3 s arm, whose 0.25 s eps calls the zone in force two ticks earlier). Measured 2026-10-21, both arms: 0 P0 escapes, no FSM edge (Normal throughout, so no autopilot ticks and no hold), 3 / 8 / 13 ticks inside the polygon (5 / 10 / 15 on the 3 s arm; the same as before, on the same path), time to safe 2.6 s (from the first tick the position is unsafe, t = 0: a stop there breaks the opening rule), never censored, goal reached, no fail-safe. The DSL lint still warns at compile time (guardrail/compiler.py time_window_lead_warnings: the start is inside the ring 1.0-2.0 s before the opening with 2.5 s needed to leave), because the position is still made illegal under the aircraft. That P0 = 0 is a RE-JUDGEMENT of the same path, not a different flight: the aircraft is inside the polygon for the same 3 / 8 / 13 ticks as on 7c9c9e6; the 6 Shield ticks are now judged the recovery, and the autopilot's P0 ticks are gone because the FSM is never entered. Measured 2026-10-22, both arms, both speeds: the 7c9c9e6 counts and time to safe exactly, 0 P0 escapes, no FSM edge. results.why:
The matrix row's "high-speed", which the 4 m/s demo policy cannot fly: policies/wgs84_taipei.yaml caps at 12 m/s, so a pilot asking 8, 12 or 20 m/s really flies 8-12 m/s - 1.2 m per 0.1 s tick - past the school-yard zone's north face (y 40.3) on a line 0.2, 0.5 or 0.8 m inside its 1 m margin ring, or exactly on it (41.3). No scenario clock, so the zone's weekday curfew is in force (absent clock = every rule active). It must never enter the ring, never exceed 12 m/s, and still get past. One face only: the zone is not square (78 x 80.6 m), so a rotation would move the line relative to the face it meets.
40.8 m at 12 m/s was a known failure from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-12 (the edge flicker below). Since the FSM counts at most one onset per second (onset limit, 2026-10-09) it passes on the shipped default, in the library and on all three nightly seeds, and on either theta reading; with the onset limit at 0 s it fails again (measured 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12). Its pin was removed on 2026-10-12. The limit is the PI's question 11 (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md, Questions for the PI): if the PI picks 0 s, the pin comes back.
RE-PINNED 2026-10-12 at the grant's 5 s forecast (the cells are deterministic, so one run measures every seed). The flicker moved: 40.5 m at 12 m/s, 40.8 m at 8 m/s and 41.1 m at 8 m/s now pass (G1>G7>G1>G7, the goal reached), and 40.5 m at 8 m/s (G1>G7>G1>G2>G5) and 40.8 m at 12 m/s (G1>G2>G5>G9) now fail by the same mechanism. Which cells flicker depends on where along the face the forecast's poses land on the ring, so it moves with the forecast; the pins follow the measurement.
PINS REMOVED 2026-11-02: the flicker still trips N-in-T (G2, a hold), but held by the autopilot the request is a steady 0 m GeofenceSlide, a repair the Shield would fly, so Loiter hands it back after T_recover (G8, guardrail/fsm.py loiter_clear "acceptable") and the pass goes on: 40.5 m at 8 m/s G1>G7>G1>G2>G8>G1>G7, 40.8 m at 12 m/s G1>G2>G8>G1>G7, the goal reached, no fail-safe. Until then G8 waited for a request with no violation at all, which never came, and the 30 s timeout (G5) sent the aircraft home though no repair was unsafe. With loiter_clear "violation_free" both cells fail again.
